pairs.question: Anxietate studens examinis exanimatus quid didicit?
pairs.derivation: The poem 'STVDIA' poses 'quid didicit?' (what did he learn?), kept with its setup 'Anxietate studens examinis exanimatus' so the subject and 'quid' have a referent. The author answers in his own voice: 'iuncti terror et error eunt' (joined terror and error go). That is the whole couplet; nothing follows to cut. Capitalized 'Iuncti' and kept terminal stop.

pairs.question: Quid petis Hansenius quaenam vitamina sumat?
pairs.answer: Promptus adest index tincta matella tibi.
pairs.derivation: The whole two-line poem. The interrogative asks which vitamins Hansenius takes; the second line answers with the means of finding out: 'promptus adest index tincta matella tibi' (a ready index is at hand for you, the stained chamber-pot). No preamble to skip; answer is the single sentence. Capitalized 'Promptus'.

pairs.question: Terrestris vitae quae debeat esse aut soleat recto propria forma viro?
pairs.answer: Institui dura multos probitate per annos, virtutis tardo culmen adire gradu, sustentare bonum, et viridi iam flore iuventae, iusta tenens vitae pro ratione mori.
pairs.derivation: Framing verb 'requiris' ('you ask'), which narrates the asking, is dropped per the framing rule, leaving the addressee's question in the author's own words and order. The reply answers it directly ('institui... mori') and is a single sentence to the only full stop; the whole reply genuinely answers what the proper form of an upright man's earthly life ought to be, so the full window is kept. Capitalized 'Institui'; '?' put on the question.

pairs.question: Exigua iuvenes habitare elegimus aede. Cur ita nos?
pairs.derivation: 'cur ita nos?' (why us so?) is kept with the preceding sentence 'Exigua iuvenes habitare elegimus aede' as verbatim setup so 'ita' has a referent (we young men chose to live in a small house). The author answers: 'nostrum quisque poeta fuit' (each of us was a poet). Stops where the next couplet turns to a new statement ('non secus everso...'). Capitalized 'Cur' and 'Nostrum'.

pairs.question: Affectus sed uter statuet mortalia fata? Divum postremo pectus habebit uter?
pairs.answer: Primus amor fuerat, fueritque amor ultimus.
pairs.derivation: Two parallel interrogatives ('which affect will settle mortal fates? which will hold the gods' heart at last?') are answered by the author: 'primus amor fuerat, fueritque amor ultimus' (love was first and will be last). Window ends at that full stop; the following 'omnes ingenii motus urget et explet amor' elaborates and is cut. Capitalized 'Affectus', 'Divum', 'Primus'.
